output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the storage compaction tuning change (FC-7710) pushed at about 23:38–23:52 on 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. In every cell the push raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disk use went from 41% to 97% and disk read waits from 9 to 205 ms. Latency crossed 150 ms within minutes of the push. The cell that skipped the push (aps-3) stayed at about 94 ms even though it had 5.8. Eu-w gateways were rolled back to 5.7 as a test and p99 didn't move. Network and traffic growth don't explain it: round-trip times are normal and GET traffic is up only 6%. Rolling back would also reopen the signature vulnerability and delay audit closure for no latency benefit.

Next step: revert FC-7710 in one cell, watch p99 and compaction backlog, then extend to the rest. Backlog is 11.2%, below the 15% level where problems start, and the projection says it won't reach 15% before 13 Nov. So use that time to find what is driving backlog growth. The Orrin migration and the lifecycle-expiry sweep are both candidates, and attribution reports on 10 Nov. Hold off on rate-limiting Orrin until then. Don't pause compaction. Confidence is high on cause, moderate on backlog source.
